maya: Hey team — hit a weird edge: streaming responses sometimes lose the Authorization header after a 307 when we relay through our proxy. Using Kotlin okhttp client. Anyone seen this?

aj: Hmm, 307s can trigger OkHttp to follow with a new request and headers may not be copied. Are you using an application interceptor or network interceptor?

maya: Application interceptor. Client builder setup:
```
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .addInterceptor(AuthInterceptor())
  .addNetworkInterceptor(LoggingInterceptor())
  .build()
```
When streaming (Server-Sent Events via ndjson) the first chunk is fine but after redirect the stream fails with 401.

tom: If the followRedirects path issues a new request at network level, only network interceptors see the subsequent request. Move auth to network interceptor or ensure `Authenticator` is used for 401/307 flows.

leah: Also check shading — we had a case where relocated okhttp classes meant our app's interceptor was not attached to the same client classpath in the private build. Could cause silent fallback to default client.

maya: Good call. How about serialization concerns? We use both Jackson for server models and Gson in the client SDK (shade-relocated). Occasionally parsing NDJSON chunks throws `NoSuchMethodError` pointing at Gson after shading.

aj: That screams classloader/relocation mismatch. Ensure the client's `build.gradle` relocates `com.google.gson` and `okhttp3` consistently and run the fatJar locally to inspect `META-INF` merges. Also verify Kotlinx vs Jackson not mixed in the same request handler.

maya: I'll try switching AuthInterceptor -> network interceptor and run a shaded integration build. Will post stacktrace if fails.

ci-bot: CI run queued for branch maya/stream-auth-fix (build 322)

aj: ping me when CI finishes, happy to review the shading rules.

maya: thanks all :heart:
